project.name: Security
project.description: Security cases raised by rules watching this deployment. Each case is one incident: assign it, investigate it, write up what you found, and close it.

tasks.title: How this project is fed
tasks.description:
Cases arrive here when a rule watching this deployment decides something crossed a line worth a person's attention. A case is the work item; the audit log behind it is the record of what happened.

A sustained run of the same thing is **one** case with a trail of recurrences inside it, not one case per event. If the case is closed and it happens again, a new case opens.

**What the fields mean.** `subject_user` and `subject_guild` are ids, not names — resolving one to a person is a platform screen, and reaching the content it points at is a break-glass grant that records why it was taken. `source_event` names the audit row this case was projected from.

**Closing a case** means somebody evaluated it and decided. Close it even when the answer is 'nothing happened' — the record that a person looked is the point. Somebody other than the subject of the event closes it.

If a case turns out to need a code change, put the finding's key in `tracker_key` so the two can be read together.

You can restructure this project however you like — rename the statuses, add fields, add your own tasks. The binding only names the project.
